chunks.arabic_text: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ خَاقَانَ، النَّهْدِيُّ، أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ، الْقَلَانِسِيُّ، الْمُلَقَّبُ "حَمْدَانُ"، كُوفِيٌّ. ضَعِيفٌ. يَرْوِي عَنِ الضُّعَفَاءِ.

translations.en: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Khāqān, al-Nahdī, Abū Jaʿfar, al-Qalānisī, who had the laqab of “Ḥamdān”. Kufan. Weak. He narrates from the weak narrators.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghada'iri’s *Kitab al-Du'afa* identifies Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Khāqān as a Kufan narrator whose reliability is diminished by his tendency to narrate from other weak sources, a common critique in Shia hadith sciences for assessing chain integrity. His multiple kunyas and nisbas (al-Nahdi, al-Qalanisi) reflect the complex onomastic traditions of Kufa, while his classification underscores the rigorous scrutiny applied to narrators who may transmit knowledge through less authoritative links.
en.seo_question: Who is Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Khāqān and what is his status in hadith sciences?

key_terms.ضَعِيفٌ: Weak (a technical term in hadith sciences indicating a narrator of moderate or lower reliability)
key_terms.الْمُلَقَّبُ: The one who has a laqab (nickname or epithet)
